units.gb: TechTrendi counts 1 GB as 1,024 MB for every network, following MTN's app (the myMTN app shows GB = MB / 1024). To show GB or a price per GB, divide mb by networks.<id>.mbPerGb (1024 for all three). Operators may count differently inside their own systems.
units.mb: bundles[].mb is the data volume in megabytes. A volume the operator prints in MB (for example AT Fuse '1024 MB', Morning Rush '1000 MB', Telecel '1000MB', MTN '460.11MB') is stored exactly as printed. A volume printed in GB (by any network, MTN included) is stored as the GB figure x 1024, so mb / 1024 gives back exactly the GB figure the operator prints.
units.gaps: mtnRates.gaps lists amounts for which MTN's tariff page publishes no rate (for example GH¢299.01 to GH¢299.99: MTN's bands are '200 to 299' then '300 to 349.99'). For those amounts say that MTN publishes no rate instead of calculating one.
units.label: bundles[].label is the data amount exactly as the operator prints it (for example AT Fuse GH¢30 '1024 MB', Telecel '1000MB', AT Unlimited 'Unlimited data'). Where the operator prints the unit only in the column header, the header's unit is added (AT Night '4.5' under 'Volume (GB)' becomes '4.5 GB'). Show it as written; calculate with mb.
units.rates: Every ghsPerMb and outOfBundlePerMb is GH¢ per MB as the operator publishes it.
units.window: bundles[].window says when a bundle can be used, if the operator restricts it to certain hours or days (for example '12 AM–4 AM', 'Saturday and Sunday', 'Sundays 6 AM–6 PM'). Such bundles are not ranked with all-day data.
units.altUssd: bundles[].altUssd is another USSD code the operator prints for the bundle (AT's Data Bundles page cards), with where it is printed.
units.borrowed: atRates.dataKredit and mtnRates.xtrabyte are borrowed data (kind 'borrowed'): the operator advances data and recovers the price plus a fee later. They are facts, never bundles, and are never compared or ranked.
units.channels: telecelRates.channels is how Telecel's data terms say their bundles can be bought (USSD codes and the Telecel Play app); families lists the families those terms cover.
units.minSpend: mtnRates.pulse.minSpend is the lowest Pulse amount MTN's help centre gives (GH¢0.07, in an article last edited 17 Jul 2024 whose volumes are older than the tariff page); amounts below it are not worked out.
units.noVolume: mb is null when the operator states no data amount: kind 'unlimited' (AT Unlimited Daily Data) and AT's Sunday Bundle (free Facebook and WhatsApp). These are never priced per GB.
units.otherSource: bundles[].otherSource (and mtnRates.midnightOtherSource for MTN Midnight data, mtnRates.pulse.otherSource for MTN Pulse) is another source from the same operator that describes the bundle differently: AT Night (AT's FAQ), MTN Kokrokoo and Midnight (MTN's Kokrokoo terms), MTN Sunday Special and Jara (their terms and MTN's help centre), MTN Data Zone (MTN's help centre), MTN Pulse (an older MTN help-centre table). The figures used are the ones the bundle's own source gives (bundles[].source); summary is the sentence shown beside it. otherSource.contradicts says what the other source disputes: 'validity' (such data is never treated as never-expiring), 'price' or 'volume'. The checker re-reads AT's FAQ on every run; MTN's terms PDFs and help centre are not re-read (see verification).
units.unconfirmed: bundles[].unconfirmed is true when the operator still lists a bundle but its newest source is more than a year old: AT Morning Rush and AT Premier Packs; MTN AFA and Association bundles; Telecel: none. asOf is that source's date. A rate band can be unconfirmed too (mtnRates.pulse.data: the GH¢5 to GH¢9.99 band, whose data rate equals the voice rate printed in the row above it). Unconfirmed bundles and bands are shown but never ranked or worked out.
units.citedSources: mtnRates.citedSources lists every MTN page, help-centre article and terms PDF the text quotes, with its date: help centre = the article's last edit (Zendesk edited_at), mtn.com.gh pages = the page's last-modified time, PDFs = the document date; 'for' names the families it is quoted for.
units.retiredFamilies: retiredFamilies (written by the checker only on a run accepted with --accept-structural-change) lists families the operator dropped, so a newer snapshot may leave them out.
units.resolvedDisputes: resolvedDisputes (written by the checker only on a run accepted with --accept-structural-change) lists disputes ({network, item, was}) a human confirmed are over, so a newer snapshot may drop an otherSource.contradicts the site showed before.
units.conditionalReason: bundles[].conditionalReason says why a conditional bundle is not for everyone: personalised (MTN Data Zone, offered only to some accounts), regional (MTN Jara, only in the regions MTN lists) or eligibility (only for a registered group: MTN AFA bundle for farmers registered with Prepeez Limited, MTN Association bundle for members of registered associations).

atRates.note: AT's tariff table lists Data Pay-As-You-Go at 18.0p per MB for every service class (One for Me, Default Bundle, Headline (Pay-As-You-Go)).

dataKredit.note: Borrowed data, not a bundle you buy: AT advances the data and recovers the price plus its "Service Fee (20%)" when you next top up. Not compared with bundles.

alsoOn.note: Same volumes, prices and total debt; this page prints no fee column.

at.Sika Kokoo: Up to 15 days. Buy another Sika Kokoo bundle within 24 hours of expiry and your leftover data rolls over. Dial *111*4#, option 1.
at.BigTime Data: Never expires, and you can gift it to friends. Dial *111*1#.
at.Morning Rush: Early-morning data for 4 AM to 7 AM, valid for 24 hours from activation (AT's FAQ). Dial *111*4# and select Morning Rush. AT's newest page for it was last updated on 6 Jul 2023, so it may no longer be on sale.
at.Night Bundle: Internet plus AT-to-AT calls, 12 AM to 4 AM only. AT calls it unlimited but lists a data amount. Dial *111#, option 4, Night Packs; AT's Data Bundles page also gives *111*4#. AT's FAQ describes these bundles differently; its version is shown under each bundle.
at.Premier Packs: Minutes or bonus airtime plus data, from AT's FAQ "AT Premier Packs". Minutes are for calls to AT and other networks; the GH¢351 and GH¢499 packs give bonus airtime that also covers calls to the USA and Canada. Buy on *703# or *111*7*2#, or in the AT app. AT's only source for them is that FAQ entry, last updated on 6 Feb 2024, so they are shown as unconfirmed and not ranked.
at.Sunday Bundle: Unlimited AT-to-AT calls plus free Facebook and WhatsApp, 6 AM to 6 PM on Sundays only. Dial *111*4*6#. AT states no data amount, so it is not ranked.
at.Family Pack (XXL): 30 days, shared with up to 3 family members. Buy another within 7 days of expiry and leftover data rolls over. Dial *111#, option 4; AT's Data Bundles page also gives *111*4#.
at.Fuse Voice & Data: Minutes for calls to all networks plus data, and it does not expire. Dial *111*2#; AT also lists *110#, *567# and the AT App.
at.Unlimited Daily Data: Unlimited data for 24 hours; the GH¢30 option adds unlimited calls to all networks. Dial *111*3*1#. Airtime only, and it cannot be gifted or shared. AT publishes no fair-usage limit, so it cannot be priced per GB and is not ranked.

mtn.Jara: Small packs of minutes, SMS and a little data for Monday to Saturday, only for prepaid customers in the regions MTN's Jara terms list: Volta, Oti, Upper East, Upper West, Bono, Bono East, Ahafo, Northern, North East and Savannah. A daily subscription that renews automatically until you stop it (send STOP to 550). Subscribe on *550#.
mtn.Pulse: MTN's youth plan. MTN aims Pulse at young customers: its Pulse page calls it 'a proposition designed to meet the communication needs of the youth in Ghana', and MTN Offers (help centre, last edited 11 Nov 2025) describes 'voice + data combo offers for young, active customers'. No MTN source says who may or may not buy it. It does not expire: MTN's Pulse terms say 'No expiry for all purchased mashups' and its help centre says 'Pulse bundles do not expire' (last edited 17 Jul 2023). To buy, dial *567# or use the myMTN app (Shop, then Mash Up): MTN's help centre gives both (last edited 17 Jul 2024), and dialling *567# opened MTN Pulse in a live test on 18 Oct 2026. Use the calculator for any amount.
mtn.Just4U: Personalised 'App Exclusive Offers' in the myMTN app ('Exclusive bundles tailored to your needs'); MTN's Just4U page says the offers 'vary from subscriber to subscriber' and gives *141# or the myMTN app. They expire and differ from customer to customer, so they are not compared here. Example offers seen in one customer's app on 17 Oct 2026; yours may differ: GH¢2.50 for 500MB (1 day), GH¢4 for 800MB (3 days), GH¢7 for 1.17GB (7 days), GH¢9 for 1.46GB (15 days).
mtn.Adwumapa: MTN's bundles for women in business on prepaid SIMs registered as female: data, social-media data, calls and doctor-on-call support, in weekly (7 days) and monthly (30 days) packs named Boafo, Adepa and Ahotor. MTN's help centre (last edited 9 Jun 2025) publishes no prices or data amounts for them, so none are listed or compared here. Dial *5060#.
mtn.Kokrokoo: Morning-only data, usable 5 AM to 8 AM daily (MTN's help centre, last edited 6 Jul 2026). MTN's help centre says it does not expire (last edited 6 Jul 2026), but MTN's Kokrokoo terms say 'Any unused data is lost after 8am', so it is not counted as never-expiring here. Dial *138#, then 3.
mtn.Midnight: Very cheap data for 12 AM to 5 AM every day. MTN's help centre says it does not expire (last edited 28 Jul 2026) and that there are 'no limits on internet activity or access to Apps' (last edited 21 Jun 2024), but MTN's Kokrokoo terms say Kokrokoo works on the 'Same principle as the Midnight Bundles' and that its unused data 'is lost after 8am'. Because MTN's own sources disagree, it is not counted as never-expiring here.
mtn.Xtrabyte: Borrowed data, not a bundle you buy: MTN's help centre says Xtrabyte lets you 'borrow airtime or data and pay later at 10% commission'. Dial *506#, option 4 'Request a data advance'. MTN's tariff page lists each advance with its 10% service fee. It is not compared with bundles or ranked here.
mtn.Data Zone: Personalised 1-day bundles, only offered if you already have an active bundle in the right price range. Not everyone can buy them. MTN's help centre says dial *135#, then option 2 for Data Zone Bundles (last edited 18 Jun 2022).
mtn.AFA bundle: MTN's bundle for farmers, run with Prepeez Limited: GH¢6 for 30 days, with or without 150 MB of data, plus minutes and SMS. Only farmers registered with Prepeez Limited can buy it. MTN's help centre on how long it lasts: 'It has a duration period of 30 days' (last edited 3 Feb 2023). Dial *1848#.
mtn.Video bundles: Data that works only on IrokoTV, DSTV and YouTube. These are the fixed amounts in the myMTN app's Video Bundles section. MTN does not state a validity. Any other amount: see the Video calculator (one flat rate per MB).
mtn.Social bundles: Data that works only on WhatsApp, Snapchat, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, WeChat and TikTok. These are the fixed amounts in the myMTN app's Social Bundles section. MTN does not state a validity. MTN's help centre (last edited 12 Aug 2024): 'Yes, you can purchase Social Bundle only via MyMTN App or *138#'. In the MyMTN app: 'Select Shop', 'Select Data', 'Select Social Bundle to purchase'. On USSD: 'Dial *138#', 'Proceed to buy bundle (No 4G bonus)', 'Select option 99 for More', 'Select option 4 for Social Bundle', 'Select option 1 to Buy for self', 'Follow service prompts to choose preferred bundle'. Menus can change. Any other amount: see the Social calculator (one flat rate per MB).
mtn.Sunday Special: Small packs of minutes, SMS and a little data that work on Sundays only (MTN Offers, help centre, last edited 11 Nov 2025: 'special voice or data deals available every Sunday only'). MTN's terms say 'Promo is open to only prepaid customers' and name no region. A weekly subscription that renews automatically until you stop it (MTN's terms: 'Weekly auto subscription applies'). Subscribe on *550#. MTN's Sunday Special page (last modified 8 Oct 2026) says 'just 65 Pesewas … inclusive Calls, Data, and SMS' and names no pack, so 65 Pesewas is not used as a price here. The introduction to MTN's Sunday Special terms (PDF dated 22 Mar 2024) says 'For only 76 Pesewas': that is the terms' Option 1 ('Cost of offer subscription is Ghc0.76': 20 minutes and 10 SMS, no data), which MTN's tariff page lists as 'Sunday Special – 20mins, 10SMS ( all net)' at 0.750. With no data it is not listed here.
mtn.Xtra4U (*203#): MTN's *203# (Xtra4U) menu offered one customer 3% off on 25 Oct 2026, e.g. 406.89 MB for GH¢2.91 instead of GH¢3, and 8.48 GB Midnight for GH¢2.91. Offers can differ by customer – dial *203# to see yours.
mtn.Association bundle: Voice, SMS and data packs for members of professional and gazetted associations that MTN has registered. MTN's help centre (last edited 24 Nov 2023) calls it 'an exclusive service offer designed for members of professional and gazetted associations in Ghana' that lets them 'purchase combo bundles (including Voice, SMS, and Data) at discounted prices', with calls inside the group (Closed User Group, CUG) while a bundle is active. To register, an association's administrator needs 'a member list, administrator ID, association documents (certificates), and a request letter'. MTN: 'Association bundle expires after 30 days'. To buy: 'Dial *5060#', then 'Select Option 2 for Association Bundles'.
mtn.Regular data (any amount): Spend any amount. The rate per MB depends on how much you spend, and it does not always fall as you spend more: some amounts buy less data than a smaller amount, so check the calculator before you pay. GH¢3, GH¢10 and GH¢399 get special rates. It does not expire: the myMTN app lists it under 'Low Cost Non Expiry Bundles'. To buy: dial *138#, then 1, then 1 (MTN's help centre: 'Dial *138# Select 1 to proceed to buy bundle (No 4G bonus) Select option 1 to Buy Data Bundles'), or use the myMTN app.

telecel.Hourly: A big burst of data that must be used within 1 hour.
telecel.Boss Plan: All-in-one packs: data, extra social data, calls to all networks and SMS. Telecel's bundles page says no expiry and 1,000 bulk SMS; its Boss Plan page says 30 days, one monthly fee and 500 SMS. Check with Telecel before you buy.
telecel.Night King: Does not expire, but only usable from 12 AM to 5 AM. Telecel's terms label it 'No Expiry (12am – 5am)'.
telecel.Special offer: 1-day deals. Telecel's terms say: "*These offers are only available on *110# and Telecel Play App".
telecel.2Moorch No Expiry: Data that never expires until you use it.
telecel.Voice & Data Combo: Calls, SMS and data together. On-net minutes are for Telecel numbers only; all-net minutes work on any Ghana network.

networkFacts.at: BigTime and Sika Kokoo give the same data whether you pay from airtime or AT Money. With no bundle, AT charges 18.0p per MB (pay-as-you-go). AT Data Kredit (*554#) lends you data, from 25 MB for GH¢0.50 to 550 MB for GH¢5; AT adds a 20% service fee and takes the total from your next top-up. It is borrowed, not bought, so it is not compared here.
networkFacts.mtn: With no bundle, MTN charges GH¢0.1145 per MB, about GH¢117.25 per GB (1 GB = 1,024 MB). Always buy a bundle first. MTN Xtrabyte (*506#, option 4) lends you data that you pay for later with a 10% commission; it is borrowed, not bought, so it is not compared here.
networkFacts.telecel: Confirm on telecel.com.gh or in the Telecel app before buying. When your data runs out, browsing stops unless you allow pay-as-you-go at 11.5p per MB (switch it on or off on *700#).

flexi.note: Type any amount from GH¢0.02 to GH¢999.99 and choose no-expiry or expiry data. Dial *700# or *110#, or use the Telecel Play app. Flexi bundles do not auto-renew.

rules.expiryRollover: All expiry bundles roll over when same bundle is purchased before expiry while different bundles co-exist and usage priority given to bundle with earliest expiry.
rules.autoRenewChoice: Customer can choose to auto-renew either no-expiry or expiry data bundles.
rules.expiryAutoRenew: Expiry bundles auto-renew at the end date of bundle expiry once customer has sufficient airtime balance. However, there is extended period after bundle expiry which allows customer to top up for bundle to auto-renew. Daily, Weekly and Monthly bundles have 1 day, 3 days and 7 days extended period respectively.

verification: Checked automatically on 26 Oct 2026 at 15:20 UTC. The checker downloaded, over plain HTTPS and without a browser, the operators' own published sources: MTN's tariff page (mtn.com.gh); the feed behind Telecel's bundles page and the feed behind its data bundle terms page (telecel.com.gh); and AT's site feed (web.airteltigo.com.gh), which holds AT's BigTime, Sika Kokoo, Night, Family Pack, Fuse, top-up, Sunday Bundle, Morning Rush and Data Kredit pages and its FAQ entries for Night, Unlimited Daily Data, Morning Rush, Sunday and Premier Packs bundles, plus the feed behind the cards on AT's Data Bundles page (for the USSD codes printed there). AT's static copy of its site data (page.json) was also downloaded and its four data tables agreed. It compared every price, volume, validity, rate and code found there with this dataset, and AT's Night Bundle page with AT's FAQ answer for the same bundle. GB figures are worked out at 1,024 MB per GB for every network. Not re-checked by this run: what the myMTN app showed (screenshots, 17 Oct 2026: the non-expiry label for regular data, the Social and Video amounts, the Kokrokoo volume and the Just4U examples; the Social and Video volumes are recomputed from MTN's tariff rates), MTN's help centre (help-center.mtn.com.gh: Midnight, Kokrokoo and Pulse validity, Pulse buying codes, minimum and older volumes, Sunday Special and Jara restrictions, Data Zone help-centre prices, Xtrabyte borrowing, how to stop auto-renewal, and the AFA, Association and Adwumapa bundles), MTN's Pulse, Jara, Sunday Special and Just4U pages, and MTN's terms-and-conditions PDFs for Kokrokoo, Pulse, Jara and Sunday Special, and how Telecel says to buy its Voice & Data Combo and Boss Plan bundles (its bundles page's purchase form and its Boss Plan page). The dates the site gives for MTN's help-centre answers are their last-edit dates, recorded on 18 Oct 2026.
